messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx/timeouts for inference endpoints detected by SLO-watch at 2026-04-22T16:02:03Z. alert id: https://alerts.redwood.example/alerts/99001

pagerduty: Paging aria (oncall-eng). Severity: P1. Channel: #incidents.

aria: oncall here. Quick check: gateway returning 502s from runner-group alpha. Initial logs show OOMKilled + segmentation faults in native inference worker. Pulling recent node logs and runner stack traces.

noah: infra chiming in. Nodes gpu-a1 and gpu-a3 show repeated oom_kill in kernel: `Out of memory: Killed process 12834 (runtime-worker) score 950` and kubelet evictions. Memory pressure seems correlated with long-context models (ctx>6k).

mira: runtime eng: stack snippet from runner: ```panic: SIGSEGV at 0x0
goroutine 42 [running]:
attention.kernel.call+0x1f3
runtime-worker/kv_cache.go:412: invalid memory read
``` Looks like a pointer used after buffer shrink under KV growth. Also seeing frequent native cuda driver errors right before OOM.

dev-support: customer ops: we have reports from two enterprise customers hitting 5xx on embeddings and long-session chat. Tickets: CS-7890, CS-7901. Preparing outbound note.

bridge-bot: Created incident bridge: https://bridges.redwood.example/INC-20260422-99001. Invited: aria, noah, mira, dev-support, sre-ops.

aria: mitigation plan options: A) divert heavy/long-context traffic to low-memory distill models (redwood-13b-compact) B) decrease gateway max_context default to 4096 for affected routes C) roll back runtime-worker 4.2 -> 4.1 D) cordon problem nodes and reschedule. Let's do A+C in parallel: divert traffic first to cut impact, then roll runtime-worker.

noah: I'll cordon gpu-a1 and gpu-a3 and drain pods. `kubectl cordon gpu-a1 && kubectl drain gpu-a1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference` -> started. Expect evictions to take ~90s per node.

mira: pushing a traffic rule now: `POST /internal/routes/shift -d '{"from":"/v1/generate","backends":[{"model":"redwood-70b","percent":70},{"model":"redwood-13b-compact","percent":30}]}'` -> starting 30% diversion to compact at 16:04Z.

dev-support: publishing internal status: "Partial outage: Elevated errors on inference endpoints. Team investigating; mitigations in flight." Will prepare external customer note if impact persists >20 minutes.

aria: checking deploy history: runtime-worker image 4.2 rolled at 02:10Z yesterday. We'll roll back to 4.1 in the inference namespace: `kubectl -n inference set image deployment/runtime-worker runtime=registry.redwood/runtime-worker:4.1` -> initiating.

sre-ops: while rollback runs, I'll add temporary gateway rule to throttle requests with context > 6k tokens and add a per-route connection cap for embeddings endpoints to reduce concurrent memory usage.

noah: cordon/drain completed; pods rescheduled. gpu-a1 showed repeated OOM on the first few scheduled pods but then stabilized after node kubelet adjusted evictions.

mira: after 30% diversion at 16:06Z, telemetry shows 5xx for redwood-70b down ~25%, overall 5xx still ~4x baseline because multiple runner pods still crash during long requests. Rollback status?

aria: runtime-worker rollback completed at 16:08Z. New pods starting. Note: rolling restart will cause short-lived 502s while pods warm up.

sre-ops: observed SIGSEGV frequency drop after rollback; OOMKilled events reduced substantially. Keeping nodes cordoned for 10 more minutes to monitor.

dev-support: customer impact summary: estimated 9.2k requests affected in window 16:02Z-16:09Z; peak 5xx rate ~11% on long-context routes. Sending targeted email to affected enterprise customers now.

mira: root cause hypothesis: regression in runtime-worker 4.2's KV growth path when combined with new async batch optimizer introduced in 4.2. The optimizer appears to free buffers prematurely under certain interleavings. We'll reproduce locally and add sanitizer checks.

aria: mitigations complete: traffic diversion + runtime rollback + node cordon/drain. I'll uncordon nodes in 15m if stable. For immediate prevention, increased default per-container memory limit for runner pods to 88% of node memory and lowered max_batch_size for long-context routes from 8 -> 3. Configs applied at 16:11Z.

noah: added autoscale alert: if any gpu node memory usage >70% for 3m, trigger scale-up policy. Also tuning kubelet eviction thresholds to be less aggressive for GPU hosts to avoid cascading evictions. Will follow up with PR.

dev-support: status page public update posted: "Mitigation in place; error rates returning to normal. Enterprise customers notified. Root cause under investigation."

mira: filing ENG-RT-3147: "runtime-worker 4.2 use-after-free in KV growth path causing segfaults/OOM" with attached logs, traces, and reproducer notes. Assigning to runtime and infra owners.

aria: handoff: I'm handing to noah for infra follow-ups and mira for runtime debug. I'll clear oncall now. Thanks team :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged and then closed by aria at 2026-04-22T16:15:56Z. Postmortem required per runbook.

bridge-bot: Bridge summary: Impact window 2026-04-22T16:02:03Z - 2026-04-22T16:12:00Z. Actions: traffic diversion, runtime-worker rollback, node cordon/drain, rate limit/connection caps. Artifacts archived to s3://incidents/2026-04-22-99001/
